blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Deploying a trained 3D Gaussian Splatting scene under shrinking compute budgets requires one primitive set to remain effective when rendered at smaller prefixes. In this continuous level of detail (LoD) setting, the challenge is to decide which Gaussians should retain capacity as the budget decreases. A pilot study on 3DGS-MCMC reconstructions shows that image complexity, computed from the input views before optimization, predicts where reconstruction error concentrates in image and 3D space. It also reveals that simple regions contain too many Gaussians and degrade as much as complex ones at lower budgets, despite being inherently cheaper to represent. Subsequently, in KoalaGS, during training we use this complexity prior to bias relocation toward poorly reconstructed areas while ensuring smooth degradation across LoDs. A primitive importance score then enables inference at low-capacity, while preserving the scene structure. Tested across three datasets, KoalaGS maintains competitive full-capacity quality while significantly improving quality across the budget spectrum, yielding smoother transitions across LoDs, and enabling faster progressive streaming.
blocks.zh: 在压缩的计算预算下部署训练有素的3D高斯电镀场景,需要一台原始设备,在较小的前缀上提供时才能继续有效。 在这种连续的详细(LOD)设置中,挑战在于决定哪个高斯人应该随着预算的减少而保留能力. 对3DGS-MCMC重建的试点研究表明,在优化前根据输入视图计算出的图像复杂度,预测重建错误集中在图像和3D空间的地方. 这也揭示了简单的地区包含太多高斯人,在低预算下退化的程度和复杂程度一样,尽管其代表的内在成本较低. 之后,在KoalaGS, 在培训期间,我们利用这种复杂性,先偏向于向重建不良的地区迁移,同时确保整个LODs的平稳退化。 原始的重要性得分后,在低容量时就可以推论,同时保留场景结构. 通过三个数据集的测试,KoalaGS保持了具有竞争力的全容量质量,同时大大改进了整个预算范围的质量,实现了更平稳地跨LODs的过渡,并能够更快地进行渐进流化。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
3D Gaussian Splatting [ 1 ] (3DGS) has made neural scene representations practical for novel view synthesis in real time. As the representation has matured, deployment under heterogeneous bandwidth and compute budgets has motivated a growing line of work on continuous level of detail (LoD) for 3DGS, where a single Gaussian set must remain useful when only a leading prefix of its primitives is retained [ 2 , 3 , 4 ] . The central problem in this setting is determining which primitives
should retain capacity as the budget shrinks. Existing methods answer it implicitly, ranking primitives by opacity [ 2 ] or by learned importance scores [ 5 ] . A structural property of the representation suggests a complementary signal. A Gaussian does not contribute equally throughout a scene, as a single primitive may account for a broad region of nearly uniform appearance yet resolve only a fraction of a visually intricate one. We contend that this spatial variation in the value of capacity is what a continuous LoD policy should exploit, and we show that it can be anticipated from the input views alone.

随着预算的收缩,应保留能力。 现有方法暗中回答,通过不透明度[2]或所学出的重要分数来排名原始人. 代表的结构属性表明一个互补信号。 一个高斯人在整个场景中的贡献并不相等,因为一个单一的原始人可能代表着一个长相几乎一致的广阔区域,但却只解决了视觉复杂区域的一小部分。 我们争辩说,能力价值的这种空间差异是持续的最低限值政策应该利用的,我们表明,仅从投入观点就可以预见到这一点。

blocks.en: We investigate this claim through a pilot study. Prior work already showed that global image complexity predicts reconstruction error in neural scene representations [ 6 ] ; however, continuous LoD requires a localized signal that identifies not only which views are difficult, but where that difficulty lies within the scene. We therefore measure the correlation between local image complexity and reconstruction quality in the 2D image plane and, after multiview projection, on the Gaussian primitives. The correlation persists across DL3DV [ 7 ] and multiple complexity functionals in both domains, supporting complexity as a spatial prior for reconstruction difficulty that is available before optimization. We then examine how 3DGS-MCMC allocates capacity with respect to this structure. Gaussian density increases with complexity, approximately exponentially in regions of high complexity, yet even visually simple regions are represented by many low-opacity Gaussians. Under truncation according to opacity, quality degrades at comparable rates in simple and complex regions, showing that opacity alone does not expose the spatial redundancy required for robust continuous LoD. Together, these observations expose a mismatch between how 3DGS-MCMC allocates capacity at full budget and how effectively that allocation is preserved under truncation.

blocks.en:
Our continuous LoD method for Gaussian Splatting addresses this mismatch. The key insight is that image complexity, which is predictive of reconstruction error,
provides an inexpensive spatial prior for allocating capacity and selecting primitives as the budget shrinks. During optimization, a relocation rule biased by complexity steers primitives toward difficult regions, while at inference an importance score modulated by complexity preserves broad primitives in simple regions and relies primarily on opacity in complex ones. A residual variance objective further discourages an abrupt degradation as the budget shrinks. We evaluate the resulting representation along three complementary axes. Our method matches the best
baselines at full capacity,
while outperforming all continuous LoD baselines across the budget spectrum, even in extremely low budget ( < 1 % <1\% ).
We show that this has great practical implication in streaming context,
where our method improves drastically the time-to-quality performance.

blocks.en: We summarize our contributions as follows: • A pilot study on 140 DL3DV scenes showing image complexity predicts where reconstruction error concentrates, while capacity is allocated in a form that truncation cannot preserve. • A continuous LoD method combining relocation biased by complexity during training, importance scoring modulated by complexity at inference, and a residual variance objective that discourages localized degradation across budgets. • An evaluation of fixed budget quality, integrated spectrum quality, and transition variance, together with a streaming study showing a better time-to-quality tradeoff.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Gaussian Splatting. 3D Gaussian Splatting transformed neural rendering by using an explicit set of anisotropic Gaussian primitives optimized for visibility-aware rasterization, enabling high-fidelity novel view synthesis at real-time frame rates [ 1 ] .
A large body of literature focuses on making this representation more stable, efficient, and deployable. On the optimization side, [ 8 ] reformulates densification as probabilistic sampling over primitives, [ 9 ] introduces structured view-adaptive anchors, [ 10 ] incorporates radiance-field-informed optimization for robust high-speed rendering, while [ 11 , 12 , 13 ] reduce training cost or remove expensive densification mechanisms under constrained budgets. A complementary [ 14 , 15 ] line compresses the trained representation itself, reducing memory footprint and rendering cost to make Gaussian scenes practical on resource-constrained devices. In parallel, other works [ 16 , 17 , 18 ] revisit the primitive parameterization, replacing or constraining 3DGS with 2D variants to improve geometric fidelity and compatibility with classical graphics pipelines. The flexibility of this representation also enables applications beyond static novel view synthesis, including dynamic scene modeling [ 19 , 20 ] , progressive and adaptive streaming [ 21 , 22 ] , mesh reconstruction [ 23 ] , or higher-level scene understanding through language grounding, segmentation, and editing [ 24 , 25 ] . Altogether, these works establish 3DGS as a general explicit scene representation. Our work employs 3DGS for deployment under
heterogeneous primitive budgets, exposing image complexity as a spatial prior over both densification and ranking.
blocks.zh:
高斯plat. 3D高斯平板化通过使用一组被优化为能见度-认知光栅化的显性异相高斯平板化的原始人来转化出神经元渲染,使高真小说取景合成以实时帧率[1].
大量文献侧重于使这种代表性更加稳定、高效和可部署。 在优化方面,[8]将密度重塑为概率取样于原始物之上,[9]引入了结构化的视距适应锚地,[10]将辐射-场-知情优化用于强力高速渲染,而[11,12,13]则在受限预算下降低培训成本或去除昂贵的密度机制. 相辅 [14,15]行会压缩训练有素的代表本身,减少内存足迹并渲染成本,使高斯的场景在受资源限制的设备上实用. 同时,其他作品 [16,17,18] 重回原始参数化,用2D变体来取而代之或限制3DGS,来提高几何忠诚度和与古典图形管道相容性. 这种表述的灵活性还使得应用能够超越静态小说取景合成,包括动态场景建模[19,20],渐进和适应性流化[21,22],网格重建[23],或者通过语言地平分,分出,和编辑[24,25]的更高级场景理解. 总体而言,这些工程建立了3DGS,作为一般的清晰场景表现. 我们的工作使用3DGS 部署在下
各种原始预算,将图像复杂性暴露为一个空间先于密度和排名。

blocks.en: Level of Detail in Gaussian Splatting. A growing body of work ports classical Level of Detail [ 26 ] into the splatting pipeline. A first category imposes explicit hierarchies over the primitive set and exposes a small number of discrete operating points [ 27 , 28 , 29 ] , with spatial divide and conquer variants scaling to kilometer sized captures [ 30 , 31 , 32 ] . A second category approximates multi budget behavior through compression and importance pruning at varying targets [ 12 , 15 ] , where each operating point is optimized independently and a new model must be retrained for every budget. A third category pursues continuous LoD over a single primitive set: [ 3 , 4 ] learn per Gaussian distance dependent opacity decay, while FlexGS [ 5 ] learns a differentiable budget conditioned selector that achieves strong quality at targeted budgets but requires a fresh forward pass at every LoD change, precluding progressive streaming. Closer to our setting, Matryoshka-GS [ 2 ] introduces a nested prefix renderable ordering trained via stochastic budget sampling, so that any leading slice yields a coherent reconstruction. Our work belongs to this last category but departs from prior approaches in how the ordering is determined: we introduce image complexity as a scene side spatial prior over both densification and ranking, and train for spatial uniformity of the residual between full capacity and prefix renders.
blocks.zh: 高斯平板电脑中的详细级别. 越来越多的工作港 古典级 详细度 [26] 进入了电镀管道。 第一类对原始的集合施加了明确的分级,并暴露出少数离散的操作点[27,28,29],空间分出并征服了可被放大到千米大小的捕获[30,31,32]. 第二类通过压缩和重要性对不同目标[12,15]进行搜索,大致了解多预算行为,其中每个操作点都独立优化,每个预算必须重新培训一个新的模型。 第三个类别在单个原始集合上追求连续LOD:[3,4] 学习每高斯距离依赖不透明衰变,而FlexGS [5] 学习一个不同的预算条件选择器,在目标预算上达到强质量,但在每次LOD变化上都需要新的前传,排除了渐进流. Matryoshka-GS [2] 推出一个嵌入式前置订货,通过花样预算抽样培训,使任何一头花样都能产生连贯的重建。 我们的工作属于最后一类,但在如何确定订单方面偏离了以往的做法:我们把图像复杂性作为场景侧面空间,先于密度和分级,并进行充分容量和前缀之间剩余部分的空间统一培训。

blocks.en: This section studies image complexity as a predictor of 3DGS reconstruction quality, computed from the input views before any optimization. The outcomes will shape our method, which must decide where to spend capacity at the moment when reconstruction error, the signal that would otherwise guide it, is not yet available. The intuition is that deploying under a primitive budget is a spatial decision. As primitives are withdrawn, some regions tolerate the loss while others do not, so the capacity that remains should sit where reconstruction error concentrates. Image complexity addresses this, since prior work [ 6 ] shows that it predicts reconstruction error and is read from the input images before optimization rather than recovered after training. What that work leaves open is whether the signal is spatial, since an image level score ranks views by difficulty but not where the error lies within them. We therefore investigate two questions: (i) Does complexity localize reconstruction error in space, across the image plane and the 3D world? (ii) Are trained models already allocating capacity where complexity predicts it should? For experimental details we refer to Sec. B.1 .
blocks.zh: 本节研究图像复杂性,作为3DGS重建质量的预测器,从输入视图计算,然后进行优化。 其结果将决定我们的方法,在重建出错、否则将引导重建出错的信号尚未出现时,必须决定将哪些能力投入使用。 直觉是,在原始预算下部署是空间决定。 随着原始人被撤回,有些地区容忍损失,而另一些地区则容忍损失,因此所剩的能力应该放在重建错误集中的地方。 图像复杂性解决了这个问题,因为前作 [6] 显示它预测重建出错,在优化之前从输入图像中读取,而不是在训练后恢复. 工作所留下的就是信号是否是空间的,因为一个图像级别得分通过难度来排列视图,而不是在其中的错误位置. 因此,我们调查两个问题:(一) 复杂性是否将空间、图像平面和三维世界的重建出错本地化? (二) 训练有素的模型是否已经按照复杂性的预测分配能力? 关于实验细节,请参考Sec.B.1。

Indeed, density control mechanism (pruning, cloning, relocation) for 3DGS are designed to increase Gaussian density where reconstruction error is higher.

blocks.en: Reporting the resulting Gaussian counts across complexity intervals in Fig. 2(a) , we observe that more complex voxels hold more Gaussians, generally following an exponential trend. blocks.en: To verify this, we implement a naive LoD strategy which preserves only the top X% of Gaussians by opacity. Varying LoD from 100% ( i.e. , full capacity) to 0.1%, in Fig. 2(b) we report the PSNR across complexity for a representative scene. While overall PSNR decreases expectedly with complexity and LoD, the study reveals another intriguing characteristic. Decreasing LoD from 100 % 100\% to 0.1 % 0.1\% lowers quality nearly equally in complex regions ( ≈ − 62 % \approx-62\% PSNR) and in simple regions ( ≈ − 58 % \approx-58\% PSNR). Moreover, PSNR fluctuations across complexity reveal uneven Gaussian opacities. Altogether, these observations show that while 3DGS-MCMC reconstructions are denser in complex regions, Gaussians remain suboptimally distributed across complexities. We further analyze how Gaussians are allocated and retained across complexity levels in Sec. D.4 .

blocks.en: 5 Experimental Results

blocks.en:
We evaluate our method on three datasets [ 33 , 34 , 35 ] and compare its performance against five baselines [ 2 , 5 , 15 , 27 , 8 ] .
Since performance of LoD-aware 3DGS may vary across LoD, it is not possible to characterize its performance by a single metric. We therefore assess our method along three complementary axes: quality at predefined LoD targets (Sec. 5.1 ), spectrum quality as the per-metric area under the curve over the full LoD sweep (Sec. 5.2 ), and intra- and inter-LOD transition variance (Sec. 5.3 ), which together capture whether quality is high, whether it is sustained across the spectrum, and whether it degrades gracefully rather than abruptly.
We further conduct an ablation in Sec. 5.4 to isolate the contribution of each component of our method. We refer the reader to Sec. C for the experimental setup description and Sec. D for additional experiments. In all tables, best results are in bold and second best are underlined .

blocks.en: We first ask whether our method delivers high quality at the operating points a user is most likely to deploy, therefore evaluating at four log-spaced budgets chosen to probe each decade of the spectrum: 100% reflects full-capacity quality, 10% a moderate compression regime relevant to deployment, 1% an aggressive reduction where ranking quality dominates and an extreme 0.1%, [typically used when initialising a streaming]. Quantitative results are reported in Tab. 2 , while separating partial-LoD methods (OctreeGS, FlexGS) as they can only be evaluated at some intervals. Qualitatives are presented in Fig. 3 , and curves are visualized in Fig. 4 . A consistent picture emerges across datasets. At full capacity , all methods are competitive (Fig. 3 , top row), with our method performing generally on par with the strongest baseline on every dataset and confirming that content-aware modifications introduce no penalty at peak fidelity. As the budget shrinks , the field separates sharply. 3DGS MCMC degrades rapidly and has already collapsed by the 1% threshold, confirming that opacity-based ranking alone cannot sustain quality under reduction. LightGaussian retains more quality than opacity-based pruning in most cases, but falls behind both MGS and ours at every reduced budget across all three datasets. OctreeGS cannot operate below its native discrete levels and it remains competitive only on the indoor Deep Blending scenes and falls behind on outdoor scenes. FlexGS, which is not prefix renderable, trades this property for higher quality near the specific operating points it was optimised for, but degrades unpredictably between them. MGS, our closest competitor, follows the same trend as our method but consistently lags behind it. Altogether, content-aware ranking yields a more robust quality versus quantity trade-off than any single-family representative, both quantitatively and visually. We report the rendering speeds in Sec. D.3 and further investigate how our importance score and densification behave jointly in Sec. D.4 .

blocks.en:
The previous section leaves open how quality evolves across the full LoD spectrum . To address this, we sample 28 operating points in [ 0.1 % , 100 % ] [0.1\%,100\%] , ten linearly spaced per interval ( [ 0.1 % , 1 % ] [0.1\%,1\%] , [ 1 % , 10 % ] [1\%,10\%] , [ 10 % , 100 % ] [10\%,100\%] ) with shared endpoints, and integrate per-metric curves with the trapezoidal rule to compute interval-wise area-under-the-curve (AUC) score, rescaled per interval for direct comparison. Since discrete methods cannot operate across the full spectrum, we focus on prefix-renderable continuous LoD methods. From results in Tab. 3 , our method consistently achieves the highest AUC.
Since the total AUC is dominated by high budgets where all methods cluster, the sub-interval breakdown is more informative. 3DGS MCMC collapses below 10% capacity, yielding the lowest sub-interval AUC across datasets and confirming that opacity-based ranking alone fails as the budget shrinks. LightGaussian improves PSNR and generally SSIM over opacity-based pruning, but remains behind MGS and ours across all metrics in the two lower-budget intervals. Our largest gain over MGS occurs precisely in the low-budget [ 0.1 % , 1 % ] [0.1\%,1\%] regime where ranking quality dominates. FlexGS performs better at [ 1 % , 10 % ] [1\%,10\%] , but it does not allow full LoD coverage.
Besides, FlexGS is outperformed by ours in other intervals, which directly results from its design as it trained for specific operating points at the cost of global consistency, producing the irregular degradation curves visible in Fig. 4 .
Overall, these results indicate that our method offers the most balanced quality versus quantity trade-off across the LoD spectrum.

blocks.en: 5.3 LoD Transition Variance
blocks.zh: 5.3 LoD 过渡差额

blocks.en:
We further assess whether our method enables fine-grained reconstruction control with smooth quality degradation. Indeed, the above mentioned metrics do not capture spatial or LoD consistency: a method that concentrates errors in localized regions may rank highly while exhibiting abrupt changes across LoDs. To analyze this, we compute per-pixel error maps following Sec. 3 and derive two complementary variance measures. Inter-LoD variance captures transitions across levels: for each patch, we take differences between error maps at consecutive LoDs, compute the variance of these residuals, and average over all patches. Low values indicate smooth rather than abrupt degradation. Intra-LoD variance measures spatial uniformity within a level: we compute the variance of each error map across patches and average over LoDs. Low values indicate that errors are evenly distributed rather than concentrated in localized regions.
Neither measure is meaningful in isolation, as uniformly poor renderings can also yield low variance. We therefore use them as a complement to the absolute quality metrics reported above. Further details are provided in Sec. E .
Results on MipNerf against MGS are reported in Fig. 5 . Across all intervals and metrics, our method exhibits lower inter-LoD variance than MGS, with the gap being most pronounced in the [ 0.1 % , 1 % ] [0.1\%,1\%] regime where budget pressure is highest and abrupt transitions are most likely to occur. A consistent reduction is also observed in intra-LoD variance, indicating that our content-aware ranking not only smooths transitions across levels but also distributes error more uniformly within each level. Taken together with the absolute and AUC results, these findings confirm that complexity-aware importance scoring yields a representation that degrades both more gracefully and more uniformly across the full LoD spectrum.

blocks.en: To isolate the individual and combined contributions of our three additions, we evaluate all combinations of content-aware densification (Dens.), content-aware importance scoring (Score), and the spatial variance loss (Var.). We report both full-capacity quality (100%) and the per-metric AUC over the LoD spectrum [ 0.1 % , 100 % ] [0.1\%,100\%] in Tab. 4 . Each component alone improves upon the baseline across all AUC metrics, except Var., which matches the baseline in AUC SSIM. Densification provides the largest standalone improvement at full capacity, while importance scoring yields the largest standalone AUC gains. blocks.en:
Our ranking naturally enables progressive streaming, where remote clients render the primitives as they arrive.
Prior 3DGS streaming systems use a few discrete quality layers [ 21 ] without characterizing how quality evolves throughout streaming.
We therefore measure time to quality : the time to reach a target rendering fidelity at fixed bandwidth.
We simulate 50 50 Mbps bandwidth (representative of 5G network), and send each primitive as raw fp32 attributes ( 236 236 bytes).
We compare against MGS [ 2 ] and 3DGS MCMC [ 8 ] , which stream incrementally like ours, and FlexGS [ 5 ] , which must restream the full set at every budget.
On the Bonsai scene of MipNerf [ 34 ] (Fig. 6 ), the prefix methods receive the full model in 49.1 49.1 s, while FlexGS needs 344 344 s, a 7.0 × 7.0\times overhead caused by restreaming. Our method reaches 25 25 dB after 1.47 1.47 s, compared to 1.96 1.96 s for MGS and 9.82 9.82 s for 3DGS MCMC, and 28 28 dB after 2.95 2.95 s, compared to 3.93 3.93 s and 14.73 14.73 s, respectively. FlexGS is also non monotone in time, dropping to about 22 22 dB in the mid budgets before recovering at full capacity. Because our importance score (Eq. 5 ) sends large primitives in simple regions first, the client sees a complete, coarse scene within the first timestamps.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: We studied how to allocate Gaussian primitives as rendering budgets shrink in continuous LoD splatting. Our pilot study showed that image complexity, accessible before any optimization, predicts spatial reconstruction error in 2D and 3D, yet trained models fail to allocate capacity accordingly in a form that a shrinking budget preserves. Building on these observations, we design a method allocating primitives based on complexity which determines their survival at inference, using a variance objective to maintain uniform error across scales. Evaluated on three datasets, our approach matches the strongest baselines at full capacity, while achieving the highest integrated quality across budgets, and degrades more gracefully, with the largest gains below 1 % 1\% capacity and faster time-to-quality in streaming.
blocks.zh: 我们研究了如何分配高斯原始人 随着预算在连续的LOD平板化中缩小。 我们的试点研究表明,图像复杂,在任何优化之前都可以获取,预测2D和3D的空间重建出错,然而经过训练的模型却未能以预算萎缩保留的方式相应分配能力. 在这些观察的基础上,我们设计了一种根据复杂性分配原始人的方法,这种方法在推论中决定了原始人的生存,使用一个差异目标来维持各种尺度上的统一出错. 对三个数据集进行评估后,我们的方法与最强的基线完全匹配,同时实现预算最高的综合质量,并更优雅地下降,最大收益低于1%的1%的容量,流水速度更快。

blocks.en: Appendix A Limitations

blocks.en: We identify three limitations that needs discussing of our approach, namely the optimization stability, the nature of our complexity prior, and view conditioning. (i) Our method inherits the stochastic relocation dynamics of 3DGS-MCMC, so results can slightly vary across runs. This variation does not alter our standing relative to prior work, as our method maintains its relative position at every capacity level and on every dataset we evaluate. The instability is moreover present to the same degree in 3DGS-MCMC and MGS, since all three build on the same relocation mechanism. (ii) The complexity prior we introduce is computed from the input images alone, and therefore captures spatial difficulty but neither view-dependent appearance nor semantic saliency. A specular highlight that shifts with viewpoint, or a small object that is salient despite low pixel complexity, receives no special treatment under our prior, and the correlations of Tab. 1 should accordingly be read as holding under standard capture conditions. (iii) Primitive selection is likewise unconditioned on the viewpoint: the formulation is neither distance- nor resolution-dependent, and is thus not designed to suppress aliasing when rendering from distant viewpoints or at reduced resolution. However, its preference for large-support primitives in simple regions may reduce the retention of subpixel primitives relative to opacity-only ranking, but this provides no antialiasing guarantee. Because we modify primitive allocation and ordering without prescribing a competing filtering mechanism, our representation remains compatible in principle with dedicated approaches such as the smoothing filter of Mip-Splatting [ 36 ] , a combination we do not evaluate here.

blocks.en: Our formulation provides global, view-independent LoD through a single primitive ordering whose prefixes define successive approximations. Unlike camera-dependent selection over a spatial hierarchy, this ordering is fixed across viewpoints and budgets, enabling progressive streaming by transmitting additional primitives as the budget increases.

blocks.en: C.1 Setup
blocks.zh: C.1 设置

blocks.en: We follow the evaluation protocol of 3DGS-MCMC [ 8 ] and report results on MipNerf360 [ 34 ] with 7 scenes, Tanks and Temples [ 35 ] with 2 scenes, and Deep Blending (DB) [ 33 ] with 2 scenes, together covering a wide range of indoor and outdoor capture conditions. We compare against five baselines spanning the design space of LoD for Gaussian Splatting. Two of them yield a prefix renderable ordering directly comparable to ours: Matryoshka Gaussian Splatting (MGS) [ 2 ] , our closest competitor, and 3DGS-MCMC [ 8 ] , which we extend with an opacity based ranking. Other two operate only at restricted points of the LoD spectrum: FlexGS [ 5 ] , a budget conditioned continuous LoD method, and Octree-GS [ 27 ] , a discrete LoD method. The last, LightGaussian [ 15 ] , is a pruning method, included to compare our ordering against post hoc decimation at equal capacity. A detailed description of each baseline and its adaptation to our protocol is provided in Sec. C.2 . All models are trained under identical conditions on NVIDIA H100 GPUs. For fair comparison we fix the total primitive budget across 3DGS-MCMC, MGS, and our method, while FlexGS and Octree-GS are reported at their native counts. We report PSNR [ 37 ] , SSIM [ 38 ] , and LPIPS [ 42 ] , which capture the complementary axes of pixel fidelity, structural preservation, and perceptual similarity.

blocks.en: C.2 Baselines
blocks.zh: C.2 基线

blocks.en: We use the gsplat reimplementation with default hyperparameters. Since 3DGS-MCMC is neither LOD-aware at training time nor designed to support budget-conditioned inference, we evaluate it under LOD by applying the simplest possible reduction strategy: at each target budget we retain the top- k k primitives ranked by opacity and discard the rest. This naive trimming establishes the baseline behaviour of an opacity-only ranking signal absent any LOD-aware training.
blocks.zh: 我们用默认超参数的gsplat重置 由于3DGS-MCMC在培训时既不了解LOD,也无意支持预算条件的推论,所以我们在LOD下通过采用尽可能简单的削减战略来评价它:在每一个目标预算中,我们保留了以不透明程度排名的上-克原始人,并抛弃了其余的. 这种天真的修剪方式确立了在没有LOD-感知训练的情况下,仅使用不透明排名信号的基线行为.

blocks.en: We use the authors original implementation. One important difference from their reported setup affects direct comparability: the original paper trains all scenes with a flat 5M-primitive budget for 50k steps. To align with our protocol and with the 3DGS-MCMC budget convention, we instead train MGS for 30k steps and adapt the primitive budget per scene to match the 3DGS allocation. All other hyperparameters follow the original implementation. Notably by doing, we observed that the stability has improved over the DB dataset over the official results.
blocks.zh: 我们使用原作者 执行。 与它们报告设置的一个重要区别影响了直接的可比性:原始的纸张会对所有场景进行训练,为50克台阶提供平坦的5M-主预算. 为了与我们的协议和3DGS-MCMC预算公约保持一致,我们转而对MGS进行30k步骤的培训,并调整每个场景的原始预算,以配合3DGS的分配. 所有其他超参数都遵循了原来的执行. 特别是,我们看到,与官方结果相比,数据库数据集的稳定性有所改善。

blocks.en: We use the authors’ original implementation and training hyperparameters without modification. FlexGS is a budget-conditioned continuous-LOD method that learns a differentiable selector mapping each primitive to a retention score for a target budget, trained in two stages: a first stage optimises the 3DGS representation, and a second stage trains the selector on top of the frozen primitives. This design trades global consistency for pointwise quality: FlexGS can outperform prefix-ranked methods at the specific budgets it is optimised for, but at the cost of (i) roughly doubled end-to-end training time, and (ii) the absence of a prefix-renderable ordering, since changing the operating LOD requires a fresh forward pass through the selector to recompute per-primitive scores rather than truncating a precomputed ranking.
blocks.zh: 我们使用作者的最初执行和训练超参数,没有修改。 FlexGS是一种有预算条件的连续LOD方法,可以学习一种不同的选择器将每个原始物映射到目标预算的保留分数,分两个阶段进行训练:第一阶段选择3DGS代表物,第二阶段训练选择器在被冻结的原始物上方. 此设计以全球一致性来交易指向质量 : FlexGS可以在它所优化的具体预算中超越前缀排名的方法,但代价是(一) 大致将端到端的训练时间翻了一番,以及(二) 缺乏前缀可服从的命令,因为改变操作的LOD需要经过选取者重新计算出每位分数,而不是切换出前缀的排名.

blocks.en: We use the authors’ original implementation and training hyperparameters without modification. Octree-GS is a discrete-LOD method that organises primitives into a fixed octree hierarchy, exposing a small number of predefined operating points corresponding to traversal depths. This design yields stable quality at its native levels but cannot interpolate between them: budgets falling between two depths are unreachable, and the coarsest level is bounded below by the structure of the hierarchy itself.
blocks.zh: 我们使用作者的最初执行和训练超参数,没有修改。 Octree-GS是一种离散-LOD方法,将原始人组织为固定的octree分级,暴露出少数与曲面深度相适应的预定义操作点. 这种设计在其本土水平上产生出稳定的质量,但不能在两者之间插出:两个深度之间的预算是无法达到的,而最短的水平由等级结构本身所约束.

blocks.en: We use the authors’ original implementation. LightGaussian is a compression method rather than an LoD one, pruning primitives by a global volumetric importance measure, fine tuning the survivors, then compacting them through spherical harmonic distillation and vector quantisation. We retain only the pruning stage, as the others reduce storage without changing the primitive count that defines our budget axis. For fairness we initialise from the same 30k step 3DGS-MCMC checkpoints as the other baselines so every method starts from an identical primitive set. We omit the recovery fine tuning, since fine tuning at each budget yields a separate optimisation run and a stored model per operating point, which is what separates pruning from a single prefix renderable ordering.
blocks.zh: 我们使用作者最初的执行。 LightGausian是一种压缩法,而不是LOD法,通过全球量子重要性测量来推倒原始人,对幸存者进行微调,再通过球形口琴分馏和向量分解来收缩. 我们只保留了修剪阶段,因为其他人减少存储而不改变决定我们预算轴的原始计数. 为了公平起见,我们从3DGS-MCMC的30k级检查站关闭,与其他基线相同,因此,每一种方法都从相同的原始组合开始。 我们省略了恢复微调,因为每个预算的微调会产生一个单独的优化运行和每个操作点存储的模型,这是从一个单一前缀可转换的订单中分离出来的.

blocks.en: In this section, we investigate how the complexity dropout rate δ \delta used during relocation (Eq. 4 ) affects reconstruction quality. With this dropout, the complexity term C ~ j \tilde{C}_{j} of a candidate g j g_{j} is set to zero with probability δ \delta , in which case g j g_{j} is not removed from the candidate set but competes for relocation based only on its opacity. The rate δ \delta therefore interpolates between two extremes: at δ = 0 \delta=0 , the complexity term is always applied and the relocation weights are fully determined by the complexity field, while at δ = 1 \delta=1 , the complexity term is always dropped and the rule reduces to the original opacity sampling p ⁡ ( g j ) = α j p(g_{j})=\alpha_{j} . We perform a value sweep δ ∈ { 0 , 0.2 , 0.4 , 0.6 , 0.8 , 1 } \delta\in\{0,0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,1\} on the outdoor Tanks and Temples [ 35 ] and the indoor Deep Blending [ 33 ] datasets, and report the metrics at full capacity and the AUC over [ 0.1 % , 100 % ] [0.1\%,100\%] (Tab. 6 ). Our default value δ = 0.2 \delta=0.2 attains the best result on all twelve entries, tied with δ = 0.4 \delta=0.4 only for SSIM at full capacity on Deep Blending. Compared to the original opacity sampling ( δ = 1 \delta=1 ), it improves the AUC PSNR by 0.14 0.14 dB on TandT ( 24.02 24.02 vs. 23.88 23.88 ) and by 0.23 0.23 dB on Deep Blending ( 29.51 29.51 vs. 29.28 29.28 ). Applying the complexity term at every step ( δ = 0 \delta=0 ) is not beneficial either, as it falls below opacity sampling on Deep Blending ( 29.00 29.00 vs. 29.28 29.28 AUC PSNR). We hypothesize that without dropout, relocation repeatedly targets the same high complexity regions, whereas occasionally dropping the complexity term lets opacity sampling reach the remaining regions. Large intermediate rates ( δ ∈ { 0.6 , 0.8 } \delta\in\{0.6,0.8\} ) perform worst on both datasets. Although the differences are small relative to the noise of the metrics, the consistency of δ = 0.2 \delta=0.2 across both datasets supports it as a robust default. We also observe more stable training with complexity dropout, especially on the indoor scenes of Deep Blending.

blocks.en: D.3 Rendering Speed
blocks.zh: D.3 渲染速度

blocks.en: We investigate the rendering speed of our method against the baselines at four levels of detail ( 100 % 100\% , 10 % 10\% , 1 % 1\% , 0.1 % 0.1\% ). We split MipNeRF360 [ 34 ] into indoor scenes (Bonsai, Counter, Kitchen, Room) and outdoor scenes (Bicycle, Garden, Stump) and report the average frame rate on a single NVIDIA H100 (Tab. 7 ). All prefix methods share an identical budget, so their primitive counts match at every level of detail and speed differences stem only from the size of the retained primitives, whereas FlexGS [ 5 ] operates with a smaller budget and is not directly comparable. At full capacity, our method is the fastest prefix method, tied with MGS indoors ( 302 302 FPS) and ahead outdoors ( 198 198 vs. 193 193 FPS). As the budget shrinks, every method accelerates, but ours does so less and saturates below 1 % 1\% , reaching 463 463 FPS indoors and 874 874 FPS outdoors at 0.1 % 0.1\% , against 829 829 and 1,151 1{,}151 FPS for MGS. We attribute this to our importance score (Eq. 5 ), which retains large primitives so that simple regions remain covered. A large primitive spans more tiles and thus costs more per frame, whereas MGS favors compact, high opacity primitives that render faster but cover less of the scene, at lower quality (Fig. 4 ). Our method is thus slower than MGS at low budgets, a cost we accept in exchange for coverage and better quality, while at equal quality it requires fewer primitives (Fig. 6 ). Reducing the per frame cost of large primitives at the lowest budgets, for instance by bounding their screen footprint, is a natural direction for future work.

blocks.en: D.4 Degradation Across Complexity Levels
blocks.zh: D.4 复杂程度的退化

blocks.en: In this section, we investigate whether the importance score (Eq. 5 ) undoes the capacity that complexity guided densification (Eq. 4 ) adds to complex regions. Since the score reduces to opacity in complex regions, primitives there are ranked with less spatial support and are therefore discarded earlier as the budget shrinks. To quantify this effect, we project the image complexity maps onto the Gaussians with the same aggregation as in our pilot study (Sec. 3 ), group the Gaussians into five complexity bins, and compare our method with MGS [ 2 ] through three statistics per bin as follows. (i) Allocation : the number of Gaussians in each bin at full capacity, which shows where densification places the primitives (Tab. 8 ). (ii) Survival rate : for each bin, the percentage of its full capacity Gaussians that are still present at a given budget, i.e. , a survival rate of 10 % 10\% means that one in ten Gaussians of that bin is kept (Fig. 10 ). (iii) Quality : we project the per pixel error maps onto the Gaussians with the same aggregation and report the average error of each bin as PSNR (Fig. 10 ). At full capacity, densification shifts the population towards complex regions, with 472.9 472.9 k Gaussians in the most complex bin [ 4 , 5 ] [4,5] against 460.5 460.5 k for MGS, and 21.1 21.1 k against 22.9 22.9 k in the simplest bin [ 0 , 1 ) [0,1) . As the budget shrinks, survival drops with complexity, as intended by the score: at 25 % 25\% budget, our method retains 33.08 % 33.08\% of the Gaussians in [ 0 , 1 ) [0,1) against 23.47 % 23.47\% in [ 4 , 5 ] [4,5] , and at 0.1 % 0.1\% the ratio grows to 2.02 % 2.02\% against 0.02 % 0.02\% . In complex bins, our method thus keeps fewer Gaussians than MGS at low budgets ( 0.02 % 0.02\% vs. 0.08 % 0.08\% in [ 4 , 5 ] [4,5] at 0.1 % 0.1\% ). This reduced survival does not translate into lower quality, as our method attains a higher PSNR than MGS in every bin and at every budget, including the most complex bin, where the gap grows from + 0.02 +0.02 dB at 100 % 100\% to + 2.25 +2.25 dB at 0.1 % 0.1\% ( 16.40 16.40 vs. 14.15 14.15 ). These results suggest that the Gaussians retained in complex regions are better placed by densification, so that the capacity removed by the score is compensated rather than reintroduced as a failure mode.

blocks.en: We complement the aggregate results of Sec. 5.4 with a breakdown at individual LoD budgets on MipNeRF360. Table 9 reports all component combinations at 100 % 100\% , 10 % 10\% , 1 % 1\% , and 0.1 % 0.1\% capacity, alongside the AUC values reported in the main paper. Among the individual components, importance scoring produces the strongest improvements across all three metrics at every reduced budget, increasing PSNR at 0.1 % 0.1\% from 14.59 14.59 to 15.94 15.94 dB. Densification also improves low-budget quality, reaching 15.68 15.68 dB at 0.1 % 0.1\% , while the variance loss alone provides smaller gains. Combining densification and scoring further raises PSNR to 16.08 16.08 dB at this budget, and adding the variance loss brings it to 16.18 16.18 dB. The complete method achieves the best results across all metrics and evaluated budgets. Its PSNR gain over the baseline increases from 0.25 0.25 dB at full capacity to 0.80 0.80 , 0.93 0.93 , and 1.59 1.59 dB at 10 % 10\% , 1 % 1\% , and 0.1 % 0.1\% , respectively, showing that the improvements are most pronounced under aggressive budget reduction.

blocks.en: In this experiment, we investigate whether the primitives retained at low budgets still cover the whole scene. A reduced budget can degrade a rendering in two ways: the scene may be represented at a coarser resolution, or parts of it may no longer be covered by any primitive, leaving "holes". We further define such holes as a pixel whose accumulated opacity is α < 0.05 \alpha<0.05 and count such pixels over all test views at 4 LoDs (100, 10, 1, 0.1). We compare against MGS [ 2 ] , our closest prefix renderable competitor, on two MipNerf360 scenes [ 34 ] : the indoor Bonsai and the outdoor Bicycle. Tab. 10 shows that coverage is preserved by both methods at high budgets and that the differences emerge as the budget shrinks. At 100 % 100\% and 10 % 10\% capacity, neither method leaves any hole. At 1 % 1\% capacity, the two methods are close on Bonsai ( 2,420 2{,}420 vs. 2,615 2{,}615 hole pixels), whereas on Bicycle MGS already leaves 5.4 × 5.4\times more holes than ours ( 11,884 11{,}884 vs. 2,204 2{,}204 ). At 0.1 % 0.1\% capacity, our method leaves fewer holes on both scenes, with MGS producing 4.0 × 4.0\times more on Bonsai ( 83,341 83{,}341 vs. 20,765 20{,}765 ) and 3.2 × 3.2\times more on Bicycle ( 116,920 116{,}920 vs. 36,009 36{,}009 ). We attribute this difference to our importance score (Eq. 5 ), which retains large primitives in simple regions, so that areas such as the background remain covered by a few large Gaussians as the budget shrinks. The same mechanism explains why the gap appears earlier on Bicycle, whose large and simple outdoor background is the first to be removed by an ordering that does not account for coverage.
